title: With the pool on and USE_TZ False, a TIME_ZONE override closes the alias's pool, and when another live wrapper of the alias (another thread's, or a copy() made before the override), which the override's reset never reaches, queries first, it rebuilds the pool from its stale cached time zone, so the overriding thread's new sessions run in the old zone (UTC instead of Africa/Nairobi, local hour 00 instead of 03); at the base the overriding thread always gets the new zone

reproduced.base: Real PostgreSQL 16.2, direct connections: after thread A and main thread B used the alias and B overrode TIME_ZONE to Africa/Nairobi, B's next session is Africa/Nairobi (hour 03) whether A or B queries first; A keeps UTC from its own cache; the same with a copy() in place of A; GT-v16's case gives Africa/Nairobi.
reproduced.head: Same steps with OPTIONS pool: when A (or the copy) queries first after the override, its wrapper rebuilds the pool and B's new session (new backend PID) is UTC, hour 00, five of five runs; when B queries first, B and A both get Africa/Nairobi; GT-v16's case gives UTC; one thread alone gives Africa/Nairobi.

not_run: No ORM read or write round trip; the demonstrated consequence is the session's TimeZone and a local-hour SQL value.
The other live wrapper was a plain threading.Thread held by events, or a copy(); no LiveServerTestCase, application thread pool or ASGI executor was run.
USE_TZ overrides were not run; with USE_TZ True and no database TIME_ZONE every wrapper's zone is UTC (read).
How often another wrapper of the alias is alive across an override was not measured.
Only Python 3.13.5, psycopg 3.1.18 (pure Python, libpq 17), psycopg-pool 3.2.1 and 3.2.0, PostgreSQL 16.2.
shipped: 5.1 (tag 2024-08-07) with the same lines 231 and 376 and the same receiver (read); main on 2026-11-10 still binds the building wrapper (read)
strongest_argument_against: GT-v16's wording and its saved fix are tied to an override in a thread that has not used the database, which the receiver skips; here the receiver runs and closes the pool as the change intends, the failure needs another live wrapper to win the race to rebuild it, and GT-v16's saved fix leaves it failing, so a reader holding GT-v16's words would not see this case until the owner widens them.

promise.whose_interface: Django's override_settings and the setting_changed reset of the database time zone (docs/topics/testing/tools.txt), with the change's pool; psycopg_pool owns only the configure hook
promise.source: docs/topics/testing/tools.txt at head, lines 1542 to 1547: Django itself resets "USE_TZ, TIME_ZONE                 Databases timezone" when those settings are overridden; announced by the change's comment at head line 363: "# Close the pool so new connections pick up the correct timezone." GT-v16's promise (rule-v4-candidates ruling 4). With Promised 7a, the overriding thread got the new zone at the base.

project-docs.query: rg -n -i 'Databases timezone|setting_changed|override_settings.*thread|thread.*override_settings|retains state|alter settings in your applications at runtime' docs (git archive of head fad334e1), query Q-a
project-docs.found: The testing guide's reset table lists "USE_TZ, TIME_ZONE" with "Databases timezone" and describes setting_changed for resetting cached state; docs/topics/settings.txt line 143 says not to alter settings in applications at runtime (example in a view); nothing limits overrides to one thread or mentions other live wrappers.

owner-docs.query: rg -n -i 'configure|reset|kwargs|close\(' on psycopg_pool docs/api/pool.rst and docs/advanced/pool.rst at tag pool-3.2.0 (3.2.1's API page byte-identical); Django's copy() and timezone_name read at head
owner-docs.found: psycopg_pool: ":param configure: A callback to configure a connection after creation."; nothing on which object supplies its values. Django's timezone_name is a cached property read from the global TIME_ZONE when USE_TZ is False.

change.query: rg -n -i 'timezone|time zone|copy\(|assume_role|role|thread|configure' upstream/change.diff (added and removed lines); the task packet title; the pull request body (empty)
change.found: The comment at line 363 "# Close the pool so new connections pick up the correct timezone." and test_connect_pool_with_timezone (one wrapper, one thread). No test with a second wrapper of the alias across an override.

maintainers.found: Nothing on overrides with several threads or on which wrapper rebuilds the pool. On PR 17594 apollo13 rejected setting the zone at every checkout ("Now we configure the connection every time on pool checkout this is certainly wrong!", 2023-12-13). Ticket 30787 (2019) shows a project wrapping override_settings(USE_TZ=False) around its whole test run.

public-code.query: gh api --method GET search/code -f q='"override_settings(TIME_ZONE" threading language:Python' -f per_page=30
public-code.unread: A bounded first page: eight hits are this investigation's own probe scripts; five project files were checked for a commit at or before the cut-off and none had one; the rest were not read. The pool option was unreleased at the cut-off, so no program could combine it with this before then. No prevalence is drawn.
public-code.found: The five project files read were all first committed in 2026 (upstream/public-code-read/dates.txt). No program before the cut-off shown overriding TIME_ZONE while another wrapper is alive.

documented-way.query: probes/N1/run.sh cases one-thread and stale-b at base and head
documented-way.found: An override in the only thread using the alias, or in a thread whose wrapper reaches the pool first, gives Africa/Nairobi at the head and at the base.

grouping_tests.note: Lines 231 and 376 with the unchanged receiver cause both; N1a also passes through line 364. fix-stale (the callback reads the zone from the settings when it opens a session) cures GT-v16's recorded case and both N1a cases; fix-checkout cures every case of both; GT-v16's saved fix (the receiver visits every alias of the current thread) leaves N1a. Sentence: new pooled sessions are set up with the cached time zone of whichever wrapper built the pool, and the reset a TIME_ZONE override triggers does not reach that wrapper.

ran: probes/N1/probe.py stale-a and stale-b at base and head (real PostgreSQL 16.2): at the head B's new session after the override is UTC when A's wrapper rebuilds the pool first and Africa/Nairobi when B's is first; at the base B is Africa/Nairobi in both orders and A keeps UTC.
stale-copy at base and head: a copy() used before the override rebuilds the pool first at the head and the main wrapper's new session is UTC; at the base it is Africa/Nairobi.
v16 and v16-idle (GT-v16's case, new and reused session) at base and head: Africa/Nairobi at the base, UTC at the head; one-thread gives Africa/Nairobi at both.
fix-v16 (GT-v16's saved fix) on every case: cures v16 and v16-idle, leaves stale-a and stale-copy UTC.
fix-stale (the pool callback reads the zone from the settings) on every case: cures v16, stale-a and stale-copy, leaves v16-idle UTC (a session opened before the override).

both-stale and fix-checkout on every case: every time-zone case gives Africa/Nairobi; fix-checkout also cures GT-v10's time zone control (v10: UTC instead of Asia/Tokyo), which the other patches leave.
Five repeats at the head of stale-a, stale-b, stale-copy and v16 gave the same results; the whole matrix gave the same table with psycopg-pool 3.2.0 and 3.2.1.

title: With the pool on, a copy() of a wrapper whose database TIME_ZONE (USE_TZ True) or OPTIONS assume_role was edited keeps the alias and shares its pool, so whichever wrapper built the pool sets up the other's sessions: the copy silently gets UTC or the login role, or the ordinary wrapper gets the copy's zone; with the role-first order every checkout times out (GT-v1); split from NC-0266123a5aa5's second case
rule_gap: Promised 1a covers settings changed at run time, and the maintainers said that is unsupported with the pool; the rule does not say whether a copy() made for tests and edited before its first query counts as changing settings, while Django's own base test does exactly that without the pool.

reproduced.base: Real PostgreSQL 16.2, direct connections: a copy with TIME_ZONE Asia/Tokyo (USE_TZ True) gets Asia/Tokyo and the ordinary wrapper UTC in either order; a copy with assume_role probe_role gets probe_role and the ordinary wrapper the login role in either order.
reproduced.head: With the pool: copy first with Asia/Tokyo, the ordinary wrapper also gets Asia/Tokyo; ordinary first, the copy gets UTC; ordinary first with the role, the copy silently gets the login role (five of five runs); copy first with the role, both time out after 2 s (GT-v1), and with GT-v1's control patch the ordinary wrapper gets probe_role.

not_run: The role-first order at the head cannot show the role effect without GT-v1's control patch; it was run with the control only.
copy(alias=...) with a new alias was read (lines 208 to 241), not run.
No ORM read or write round trip.
Grouping against GT-v15 and GT-v2 was not run.
How often code copies a pooled wrapper and edits its settings was not measured.
shipped: 5.1 (tag 2024-08-07) with the same alias-only lookup and bound callback (read); unchanged on main 2026-11-10 (read)
strongest_argument_against: At the base Django's own test_connect_role copied the connection and gave the copy its own assume_role, which worked, the database TIME_ZONE and assume_role are documented settings, and nothing in the pool documentation warns that a copy's settings are ignored; the maintainers' statements are hedged and were about settings changed after the fact, not a copy configured before its first query.

promise.whose_interface: Django's undocumented BaseDatabaseWrapper.copy() (docstring: "For tests that require two connections to the same database.") used with its settings_dict TIME_ZONE or OPTIONS assume_role edited while the alias's pool exists

project-docs.query: rg -n '\.copy\(|copy of this connection|two connections to the same database|settings_dict' docs and rg -n -i 'assume_role|connection pool|postgresql-pool|DATABASE-TIME_ZONE' docs (git archive of head fad334e1), queries Q-b and Q-c
project-docs.found: No page names DatabaseWrapper.copy(); docs/topics/settings.txt line 143: "You shouldn't alter settings in your applications at runtime."; the database TIME_ZONE and assume_role are documented as DATABASES settings, so a second alias is the documented way to have other settings; the pool section says nothing about copies or edited settings.

owner-docs.query: rg -n -i 'configure|reset|kwargs|close\(' on psycopg_pool docs/api/pool.rst and docs/advanced/pool.rst at tag pool-3.2.0 (3.2.1's API page byte-identical); Django's copy() and timezone_name read at head
owner-docs.found: Django owns copy(): "Return a copy of this connection. For tests that require two connections to the same database." psycopg_pool: ":param configure: A callback to configure a connection after creation."; nothing on a pool shared by objects with different settings.

public-code.query: gh api --method GET search/code -f q='"connection.copy()" "assume_role" language:Python' -f per_page=30 and -f q='"connection.copy()" "settings_dict" "TIME_ZONE" language:Python' -f per_page=30
public-code.unread: 75 and 220 files, nearly all copies of Django's own test suite; five files outside Django were read with their commit dates (upstream/public-code-read/dates.txt). A search count is not a practice.
public-code.found: Three of the five existed before the cut-off (django-clickhouse-backend 2023-10-04, django-sqlserver 2017-07-08, django-async 2017-11-13), all copies of Django's backend tests that copy the connection, two editing the copy's AUTOCOMMIT or isolation level, none with a pool; the pool option was unreleased then.

documented-way.query: probes/N1/run.sh cases alias-tz and alias-role at base, head and the patched trees; alias-role also with GT-v1's control patch
documented-way.found: A second alias with TIME_ZONE Asia/Tokyo gets its own pool and its own zone at the head; a second alias with assume_role fails at the head with GT-v1's timeout and gets probe_role with GT-v1's control patch.

grouping_tests.note: Both pass through line 231 and, for the zone, line 376; GT-v16 also needs the unchanged receiver, N1b the alias-only lookup (208, 241) and for the role lines 380 to 381. Each smallest fix (fix-v16, fix-copy) cures only its own cases; only both, or the broad fix-checkout, cure both, and fix-checkout also cures GT-v10's time zone case. A cause sentence true of both (sessions are set up from the wrapper that built the pool, not the one asking) is equally true of GT-v15 and GT-v2, which the owner kept separate. The role-first failure at the head is GT-v1's symptom.

ran: probes/N1/probe.py copy-tz-1 and copy-tz-2 (USE_TZ True) at base and head: at the base each wrapper gets its own zone; at the head the wrapper that built the pool sets the other's zone in both orders.
copy-role-1 and copy-role-2 at base and head: at the base each gets its own role; at the head ordinary-first gives the copy the login role silently and copy-first times out for both (GT-v1).

The same role cases on six trees with GT-v1's control patch: head-v1 gives the ordinary wrapper the copy's role when the copy is first; fix-copy-v1, fix-checkout-v1 and both-copy-v1 give each wrapper its own role.
fix-v16, fix-copy, both-copy and fix-checkout on every case: fix-v16 cures only GT-v16's case; fix-copy only the copy cases; both and fix-checkout cure all.
alias-tz and alias-role at base and head: a second alias gets its own pool and zone at the head; with a role it times out (GT-v1) and works with the control patch.
Five repeats at the head of copy-tz-1, copy-tz-2 and copy-role-2 gave the same results; psycopg-pool 3.2.0 and 3.2.1 gave the same table.
